subject.title: Session lane starvation: followup drain monopolizes session lane, blocks inbound dispatch for 20-30min

question: Should same-session user-visible inbound turns always preempt or defer background/follow-up work, and should the permanent fix be a structural foreground/background split or a bounded follow-up drain cap?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the correct invariant affects session ordering, STOP semantics, transcript state, and channel delivery, so automation should not choose the scheduler policy without owner intent.

options.title: Foreground-user scheduler invariant
options.body: Make user-visible inbound turns the privileged foreground class, defer or abort background/follow-up work when necessary, and keep background/system events best-effort.

options.title: Bound consecutive follow-up drain
options.body: Limit the number or time budget of consecutive follow-up turns before yielding to newly queued inbound work, with lower architectural churn but weaker STOP semantics.

options.title: Wait for slice PRs only
options.body: Land narrow fixes such as related admission or cron-binding PRs first and leave the broader fairness invariant unresolved for a later design pass.

recommendation.title: Foreground-user scheduler invariant
recommendation.body: Make user-visible inbound turns the privileged foreground class, defer or abort background/follow-up work when necessary, and keep background/system events best-effort.
